lines.text: You kept driving. You still think about it.
lines.cap:
YOU KEPT DRIVING.
YOU STILL THINK ABOUT IT.

lines.text: Your car is going to die. You only choose where.
lines.cap:
YOUR CAR IS GOING TO DIE.
YOU ONLY CHOOSE WHERE.

lines.text: Eleven miles left. Every road south ends at one bridge.
lines.cap:
11 MILES LEFT.
EVERY ROAD ENDS AT ONE BRIDGE.

lines.text: And the bridge is a six mile car park.
lines.cap:
AND THE BRIDGE IS A
SIX MILE CAR PARK.

lines.text: So you stop choosing roads. You walk the railway.
lines.cap:
SO YOU STOP CHOOSING ROADS.
YOU WALK THE RAILWAY.

lines.text: Elevated. Fenced both sides. Dead straight. And empty.
Recovery in six days. Transit south. Avoid all crossings.
Rule one. Walk the sleepers, not the stones.
Rule two. Count bridges, not miles.
Rule three. Never shelter anywhere with one door.
Good news. Eleven miles in, a freight yard. A locomotive, idling.
Bad news. Between you and it is a signal box. One room. One door.
lines.cap:
BAD NEWS. A SIGNAL BOX.
ONE ROOM. ONE DOOR.

lines.text: Four fifty five. You go in for the yard keys.
lines.cap:
4:55 AM. YOU GO IN
FOR THE YARD KEYS.

lines.text: And the staircase creaks behind you.
Driver? I've been holding this train nine days. Come down.
lines.cap:
“DRIVER? I'VE BEEN HOLDING
THIS TRAIN NINE DAYS.”

lines.text: All rail staff evacuated on day one.
Then the loop plays past the point it has ever reached.
lines.cap:
THEN THE LOOP PLAYS PAST
WHERE IT HAS EVER REACHED.

lines.text: It isn't a rescue message. It's a warning.
lines.cap:
IT ISN'T A RESCUE MESSAGE.
IT'S A WARNING.

lines.text: Do you go down the stairs?
